Aquatics programs Browse the schedule of upcoming Aquatics programs. Go to the Aquatics schedules Aquatics programs All of our aquatics programs are HIGH FIVE certified. Learn to swim The Town of Oakville offers lessons according to the Lifesaving Society Swim for Life program. Age guidelines Children must be the age required for the level they are taking by the program start date. Children who are five years-old do not need to complete all preschool levels before moving to the Swimmer programs. Children who have completed the Preschool E and who are five years old should enrol in Swimmer 2. Leadership courses and recertification How to become a Lifeguard and Swimming Instructor The following Aquatics Leadership and First Aid courses must be completed successfully to qualify for a range of aquatics positions : Basic First Aid with CPR-C and AED – no prerequisites required Bronze Star – completed Swimmer 10 (Star Patrol) recommended Bronze Medallion – minimum age 13 or Bronze Star required Bronze Cross and Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C and AED – Bronze Medallion and Emergency First Aid or Basic First Aid with CPR-C and AED required Swim and Lifesaving Instructors – minimum age 15 and Bronze Cross at course start required National Lifeguard (NL) – minimum age 15 with Bronze Cross and Standard First Aid or Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C and AED at course start required Download the Aquatics Leadership Ladder (pdf). Transfers and withdrawals Transfers and withdrawals must be completed at least four full days before the program starts. For example, if your program starts at 9 a.m., you must withdraw by 9 a.m. four days in advance. No credits or refunds will be issued once you are within four days of the start time or after the program begins. Re-certification Re-certification courses include Bronze Cross Challenge Exam (ages 13+), Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C and AED Re-certification, and National Lifeguard Re-certification (ages 16+). Your original award card must be shown to the examiner to participate in the re-certification test. Challenge exams The Bronze Medallion Challenge Exam (ages 13+) is for Bronze Medallion candidates who need to re-certify their award, or for swimmers who are looking to challenge the exam as a self-presented candidate. Re-certification candidates must bring their original certification card Challenge candidates must bring proof of course prerequisites: Bronze Star award or proof of age (candidate must be 13 years or older on exam date). The Bronze Cross Challenge Exam is for Bronze Cross candidates who need to re-certify their award, or for swimmers who are looking to challenge the exam as a self-presented candidate. Re-certification candidates must bring their original certification card Challenge candidates must bring proof of course prerequisites: Bronze Medallion award and Emergency First Aid with CPR (Level B) or Basic First Aid with CPR-C and AED Aquatics Leadership Development courses The following courses are offered to help participants develop their leadership skills but are not prerequisites. Leadership Skill Session (ages 10+) Practice time for participants enrolled in advanced aquatic leadership courses. Instructors will be available to provide guidance and support with specific skills upon request. Pre-National Lifeguard Prerequisite: Bronze Cross If you have completed Bronze Cross and are waiting to take your National Lifeguard (NL) certification, Pre-National Lifeguard will reinforce the water rescue skills learned in Bronze Cross and introduce new skills that will be part of the NL program. You'll work in pairs and on your own. Looking for additional swimming opportunities? Participants ages 11–17 can attend Free Youth Length Swims to improve endurance and swimming fitness to prepare for aquatic leadership courses and lifesaving certifications. Registration If you would like to register for a program, visit our Registered Programs page. Visit the Program Guidelines page for information about registration timelines. Swim to Survive school programs Lifesaving Society’s Canadian Swim to Survive standard defines the essential minimum skills required to survive an unexpected fall into deep water. Swim to Survive programs Swim to Survive classes are provided as part of the Grade 3 public school and the Grade 4 Catholic school curriculum. Students are bused to a Town of Oakville pool for three in-water lessons focusing on the sequence of three skills: roll into deep water; tread water for one-minute; and swim 50 metres. Fees are subject to grant funding. Please call for rates. Swim to Survive Plus Swim to Survive Plus builds on the skills taught in Swim to Survive. Geared toward presenting real-life situations for students in Grade 7, participants will learn: How to roll, tread and swim with clothes on. How to help a friend in deep water without putting themselves in danger (talk, reach, throw). Basic physical fitness concepts through interval training and a fitness swim. Fees are subject to grant funding. Please call for rates. Pool rentals and programs for schools Pool rental and programs can be created for Grades 1 through 12. We offer lessons, water safety or fun swim programs based on interest and skill level. Email bookafacility@oakville.ca or visit the Facility Rentals page for details. Contact Email swimtosurvive@oakville.ca or call 905-845-6601, ext. 3466. Program guidelines For information about things you should know before attending your course, visit the Program Guidelines page. FAQ Reviews Fees Dear Parents Programs Fun in the Jungle Chef’s Kitchen Blog Wait List How Early Swim Lessons Build Confidence and Safety in Young Kids January 30, 2026 Saurabh Off Activities , Family , Health and Safety Learning to swim ranks among the most important life skills children can develop. Early swim lessons for kids provide far more than just the ability to move through water—they build confidence, promote physical development, and teach critical safety skills that can save lives. For families in Oakville, numerous quality programs offer age-appropriate instruction that makes water safety accessible to children from infancy through school age. Why Early Swim Lessons for Kids Matter Drowning remains a leading cause of accidental death in young children, making water safety education essential. Early swim lessons for kids teach respect for water while building skills that significantly reduce drowning risk. Even basic water competency—the ability to enter water, surface, turn, and reach safety—dramatically improves a child’s chances of surviving unexpected water immersion. Beyond safety, swim lessons for kids offer developmental benefits that extend far beyond the pool. Swimming engages the entire body, building strength, coordination, and endurance. The bilateral movements required for swimming strokes enhance brain development and motor planning skills in ways that few other activities provide. Water activities also support emotional development. Successfully mastering swimming skills builds self-confidence as children overcome fears and achieve goals. The structured environment of swim lessons teaches children to follow instructions, wait their turn, and persist through challenges—all valuable life skills. When to Start Swim Lessons The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends swim lessons for kids starting around age 1, though parent-child water familiarization classes can begin as early as 6 months. These early classes don’t teach formal swimming but help babies become comfortable in water while building parent confidence in handling infants in aquatic environments. Toddlers ages 1-3 benefit from classes that teach water safety rules and basic skills like blowing bubbles, floating, and moving through water with support. Most children develop the physical coordination necessary for independent swimming around ages 4-5, when formal stroke instruction becomes more effective. However, every child develops differently. Some children show readiness for swim lessons earlier while others need more time. Consider your child’s comfort level, ability to follow instructions, and physical development when deciding when to start lessons. What to Look for in Quality Swim Lessons Effective swim lessons for kids prioritize safety while making learning enjoyable. Look for programs with certified instructors who have training in child development and water safety. Small class sizes ensure individual attention, especially for younger children who need more support. Quality programs assess each child’s abilities and place them in appropriate levels rather than grouping solely by age. Progressive curricula that build skills systematically help children advance confidently from one level to the next. The facility itself matters too. Warm water temperatures (82-86°F for young children) make lessons more comfortable and allow children to focus on learning rather than feeling cold. Clean, well-maintained pools with proper supervision demonstrate commitment to safety and quality. Swim Lessons for Kids in Oakville Oakville offers excellent options for families seeking quality swim instruction for young children. Each program brings unique approaches and benefits. Town of Oakville Aquatics Programs The Town of Oakville Recreation and Culture operates swimming programs at multiple locations including Iroquois Ridge Community Centre, Glen Abbey Recreation Centre, and River Oaks Community Centre. These municipal programs offer affordable swim lessons for kids from parent-child classes through advanced levels, following the Red Cross swimming curriculum. YMCA of Oakville The YMCA of Oakville provides comprehensive swim programming based on the Lifesaving Society’s Swim for Life program. Their approach emphasizes fun, safety, and skill development with options for parent-child classes, preschool lessons, and youth swimming. The YMCA offers financial assistance to families who need support accessing programs. Mississauga and West Shore Swim School (Oakville Location) MWSS Oakville specializes in year-round swim instruction with small class sizes and warm water pools. Their progressive curriculum serves children from 6 months through teens, with emphasis on building water confidence and safety skills alongside technical swimming ability. Goldfish Swim School Goldfish Swim School Oakville offers a tropical-themed environment with a 90-degree pool perfect for young children. Their play-based approach makes swim lessons for kids fun while teaching essential water safety and swimming skills. Classes run year-round with flexible scheduling options. Atlantis School of Swim Atlantis School of Swim provides personalized instruction in small group settings. Their program focuses on building strong foundations in water safety and swimming technique, with classes available for babies through adults. British Swim School British Swim School at TownePlace Suites brings a survival-first approach to swim lessons, teaching children what to do if they accidentally fall into water before focusing on stroke development. Their gentle, encouraging method works well for children who are nervous about water. Preparing Your Child for Swim Lessons Help your child start swim lessons for kids confidently by preparing them for what to expect. Talk positively about swimming, read books about learning to swim, and if possible, visit the pool before the first lesson so your child becomes familiar with the environment. Practice basic skills at bath time like blowing bubbles, getting faces wet, and floating on backs (with full support, of course). These playful preparations reduce anxiety about trying new things in swim class. Choose appropriate swimwear that fits well and won’t slide or come off during activity. Consider swim diapers for children who aren’t potty trained, and bring towels, goggles if your child prefers them, and dry clothes for after class. Supporting Progress at Home Reinforce swim lessons for kids by visiting pools for recreational swimming between classes. Practice skills learned in lessons, but keep it fun and pressure-free. Playing in water builds comfort and confidence that supports formal instruction. Never leave children unattended near water, even after they’ve started swim lessons. Swimming ability doesn’t eliminate drowning risk, and constant supervision remains essential. Layers of protection—fencing around pools, locked gates, and vigilant adult supervision—work together to keep children safe. Building Lifelong Water Safety The benefits of early swim lessons for kids extend throughout life. Children who learn to swim young often develop lifelong love of aquatic activities, supporting physical fitness and providing recreational enjoyment for years to come. Perhaps most importantly, swim lessons give children skills that could save their lives or the lives of others. The confidence and competence built through early swimming instruction creates safer, more capable individuals who can enjoy water activities while respecting water’s power. Whether you choose municipal programs, specialized swim schools, or private instruction, investing in swim lessons for kids provides returns in safety, confidence, and physical development that last a lifetime. Aquatics programs Browse the schedule of upcoming Aquatics programs. Go to the Aquatics schedules Aquatics programs All of our aquatics programs are HIGH FIVE certified. Learn to swim The Town of Oakville offers lessons according to the Lifesaving Society Swim for Life program. Age guidelines Children must be the age required for the level they are taking by the program start date. Children who are five years-old do not need to complete all preschool levels before moving to the Swimmer programs. Children who have completed the Preschool E and who are five years old should enrol in Swimmer 2. Leadership courses and recertification How to become a Lifeguard and Swimming Instructor The following Aquatics Leadership and First Aid courses must be completed successfully to qualify for a range of aquatics positions : Basic First Aid with CPR-C and AED – no prerequisites required Bronze Star – completed Swimmer 10 (Star Patrol) recommended Bronze Medallion – minimum age 13 or Bronze Star required Bronze Cross and Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C and AED – Bronze Medallion and Emergency First Aid or Basic First Aid with CPR-C and AED required Swim and Lifesaving Instructors – minimum age 15 and Bronze Cross at course start required National Lifeguard (NL) – minimum age 15 with Bronze Cross and Standard First Aid or Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C and AED at course start required Download the Aquatics Leadership Ladder (pdf). Transfers and withdrawals Transfers and withdrawals must be completed at least four full days before the program starts. For example, if your program starts at 9 a.m., you must withdraw by 9 a.m. four days in advance. No credits or refunds will be issued once you are within four days of the start time or after the program begins. Re-certification Re-certification courses include Bronze Cross Challenge Exam (ages 13+), Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C and AED Re-certification, and National Lifeguard Re-certification (ages 16+). Your original award card must be shown to the examiner to participate in the re-certification test. Challenge exams The Bronze Medallion Challenge Exam (ages 13+) is for Bronze Medallion candidates who need to re-certify their award, or for swimmers who are looking to challenge the exam as a self-presented candidate. Re-certification candidates must bring their original certification card Challenge candidates must bring proof of course prerequisites: Bronze Star award or proof of age (candidate must be 13 years or older on exam date). The Bronze Cross Challenge Exam is for Bronze Cross candidates who need to re-certify their award, or for swimmers who are looking to challenge the exam as a self-presented candidate. Re-certification candidates must bring their original certification card Challenge candidates must bring proof of course prerequisites: Bronze Medallion award and Emergency First Aid with CPR (Level B) or Basic First Aid with CPR-C and AED Aquatics Leadership Development courses The following courses are offered to help participants develop their leadership skills but are not prerequisites. Leadership Skill Session (ages 10+) Practice time for participants enrolled in advanced aquatic leadership courses. Instructors will be available to provide guidance and support with specific skills upon request. Pre-National Lifeguard Prerequisite: Bronze Cross If you have completed Bronze Cross and are waiting to take your National Lifeguard (NL) certification, Pre-National Lifeguard will reinforce the water rescue skills learned in Bronze Cross and introduce new skills that will be part of the NL program. You'll work in pairs and on your own. Looking for additional swimming opportunities? Participants ages 11–17 can attend Free Youth Length Swims to improve endurance and swimming fitness to prepare for aquatic leadership courses and lifesaving certifications. Registration If you would like to register for a program, visit our Registered Programs page. Visit the Program Guidelines page for information about registration timelines. Swim to Survive school programs Lifesaving Society’s Canadian Swim to Survive standard defines the essential minimum skills required to survive an unexpected fall into deep water. Swim to Survive programs Swim to Survive classes are provided as part of the Grade 3 public school and the Grade 4 Catholic school curriculum. Students are bused to a Town of Oakville pool for three in-water lessons focusing on the sequence of three skills: roll into deep water; tread water for one-minute; and swim 50 metres. Fees are subject to grant funding. Please call for rates. Swim to Survive Plus Swim to Survive Plus builds on the skills taught in Swim to Survive. Geared toward presenting real-life situations for students in Grade 7, participants will learn: How to roll, tread and swim with clothes on. How to help a friend in deep water without putting themselves in danger (talk, reach, throw). Basic physical fitness concepts through interval training and a fitness swim. Fees are subject to grant funding. Please call for rates. Pool rentals and programs for schools Pool rental and programs can be created for Grades 1 through 12. We offer lessons, water safety or fun swim programs based on interest and skill level. Email bookafacility@oakville.ca or visit the Facility Rentals page for details. FAQ Reviews Fees Dear Parents Programs Fun in the Jungle Chef’s Kitchen Blog Wait List How Early Swim Lessons Build Confidence and Safety in Young Kids January 30, 2026 Saurabh Off Activities , Family , Health and Safety Learning to swim ranks among the most important life skills children can develop. Early swim lessons for kids provide far more than just the ability to move through water—they build confidence, promote physical development, and teach critical safety skills that can save lives. For families in Oakville, numerous quality programs offer age-appropriate instruction that makes water safety accessible to children from infancy through school age. Why Early Swim Lessons for Kids Matter Drowning remains a leading cause of accidental death in young children, making water safety education essential. Early swim lessons for kids teach respect for water while building skills that significantly reduce drowning risk. Even basic water competency—the ability to enter water, surface, turn, and reach safety—dramatically improves a child’s chances of surviving unexpected water immersion. Beyond safety, swim lessons for kids offer developmental benefits that extend far beyond the pool. Swimming engages the entire body, building strength, coordination, and endurance. The bilateral movements required for swimming strokes enhance brain development and motor planning skills in ways that few other activities provide. Water activities also support emotional development. Successfully mastering swimming skills builds self-confidence as children overcome fears and achieve goals. The structured environment of swim lessons teaches children to follow instructions, wait their turn, and persist through challenges—all valuable life skills. When to Start Swim Lessons The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends swim lessons for kids starting around age 1, though parent-child water familiarization classes can begin as early as 6 months. These early classes don’t teach formal swimming but help babies become comfortable in water while building parent confidence in handling infants in aquatic environments. Toddlers ages 1-3 benefit from classes that teach water safety rules and basic skills like blowing bubbles, floating, and moving through water with support. Most children develop the physical coordination necessary for independent swimming around ages 4-5, when formal stroke instruction becomes more effective. However, every child develops differently. Some children show readiness for swim lessons earlier while others need more time. Consider your child’s comfort level, ability to follow instructions, and physical development when deciding when to start lessons. What to Look for in Quality Swim Lessons Effective swim lessons for kids prioritize safety while making learning enjoyable. Look for programs with certified instructors who have training in child development and water safety. Small class sizes ensure individual attention, especially for younger children who need more support. Quality programs assess each child’s abilities and place them in appropriate levels rather than grouping solely by age. Progressive curricula that build skills systematically help children advance confidently from one level to the next. The facility itself matters too. Warm water temperatures (82-86°F for young children) make lessons more comfortable and allow children to focus on learning rather than feeling cold. Clean, well-maintained pools with proper supervision demonstrate commitment to safety and quality. Swim Lessons for Kids in Oakville Oakville offers excellent options for families seeking quality swim instruction for young children. Each program brings unique approaches and benefits. Town of Oakville Aquatics Programs The Town of Oakville Recreation and Culture operates swimming programs at multiple locations including Iroquois Ridge Community Centre, Glen Abbey Recreation Centre, and River Oaks Community Centre. These municipal programs offer affordable swim lessons for kids from parent-child classes through advanced levels, following the Red Cross swimming curriculum. YMCA of Oakville The YMCA of Oakville provides comprehensive swim programming based on the Lifesaving Society’s Swim for Life program. Their approach emphasizes fun, safety, and skill development with options for parent-child classes, preschool lessons, and youth swimming. The YMCA offers financial assistance to families who need support accessing programs. Mississauga and West Shore Swim School (Oakville Location) MWSS Oakville specializes in year-round swim instruction with small class sizes and warm water pools. Their progressive curriculum serves children from 6 months through teens, with emphasis on building water confidence and safety skills alongside technical swimming ability. Goldfish Swim School Goldfish Swim School Oakville offers a tropical-themed environment with a 90-degree pool perfect for young children. Their play-based approach makes swim lessons for kids fun while teaching essential water safety and swimming skills. Classes run year-round with flexible scheduling options. Atlantis School of Swim Atlantis School of Swim provides personalized instruction in small group settings. Their program focuses on building strong foundations in water safety and swimming technique, with classes available for babies through adults. British Swim School British Swim School at TownePlace Suites brings a survival-first approach to swim lessons, teaching children what to do if they accidentally fall into water before focusing on stroke development. Their gentle, encouraging method works well for children who are nervous about water. Preparing Your Child for Swim Lessons Help your child start swim lessons for kids confidently by preparing them for what to expect. Talk positively about swimming, read books about learning to swim, and if possible, visit the pool before the first lesson so your child becomes familiar with the environment. Practice basic skills at bath time like blowing bubbles, getting faces wet, and floating on backs (with full support, of course). These playful preparations reduce anxiety about trying new things in swim class. Choose appropriate swimwear that fits well and won’t slide or come off during activity. Consider swim diapers for children who aren’t potty trained, and bring towels, goggles if your child prefers them, and dry clothes for after class. Supporting Progress at Home Reinforce swim lessons for kids by visiting pools for recreational swimming between classes. Practice skills learned in lessons, but keep it fun and pressure-free. Playing in water builds comfort and confidence that supports formal instruction. Never leave children unattended near water, even after they’ve started swim lessons. Swimming ability doesn’t eliminate drowning risk, and constant supervision remains essential. Layers of protection—fencing around pools, locked gates, and vigilant adult supervision—work together to keep children safe. Building Lifelong Water Safety The benefits of early swim lessons for kids extend throughout life. Children who learn to swim young often develop lifelong love of aquatic activities, supporting physical fitness and providing recreational enjoyment for years to come. Perhaps most importantly, swim lessons give children skills that could save their lives or the lives of others. The confidence and competence built through early swimming instruction creates safer, more capable individuals who can enjoy water activities while respecting water’s power. Whether you choose municipal programs, specialized swim schools, or private instruction, investing in swim lessons for kids provides returns in safety, confidence, and physical development that last a lifetime.
